newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Deus Pinheiro to present refugee action plan.
newsitem.headline: Deus Pinheiro to present refugee action plan.

text.p: Joao de Deus Pinheiro, the European Union's development aid commissioner, said on Wednesday he will propose a general action plan next week to resettle refugees in the Great Lakes region of Africa.
Tens of thousands more Hutu refugees, who fled massacres two years ago, are reportedly heading through eastern Zaire to Rwanda, the possible vanguard of a second mass exodus.
"There must not be a gap between emergency humanitarian aid and rehabilitation aid," Deus Pinheiro told a news conference.
The EU aid would be used to help guarantee law and order and to provide housing, health care and jobs for the refugees.
"We must act quickly," he added, saying he hoped to put a proposal, based on an assessment from an EU team in the region, to EU foreign ministers on Monday.
Officials said the aid would probably be provided from spare resources in the European Development Fund and could therefore be committed quickly.
Deus Pinheiro said he believed a multinational force was still necessary in the region, though perhaps of a smaller size.
"The fact that 500,000 have returned to Rwanda does not mean that the problem is solved. We still have some 700,000 in Zaire and I imagine in a very difficult situation," he said.
Massive numbers of refugees, Rwandan, Burundian and Zairean, have migrated westwards from camps in Kivu, eastern Zaire.
"The only hope we have of trying to see where they are and trying to help them is through a force," he said.
Although things were moving reasonably well in Rwanda, Deus Pinheiro said the situation was much more serious in Burundi.
"Reports...indicate that many of the (Hutu) refugees that entered Burundi have been slaughtered," he said.
A huge number of refugees had also reportedly continued into Tanzania and were trying to settle near the frontier, he said.
"We hope this will not take place as it will be a repetition of what happened in Kivu. We are very concerned about the situation," he said.
On Tuesday, Burundian Prime Minister Pascal Firmin Ndimira said the situation had improved.
"There is a net improvement in security in towns and some rural areas," he told reporters, adding however that armed rebels were causing difficulties in some regions.
